stories.title: Israel's election looks deadlocked, with a narrow exit-poll lead for the opposition
stories.summary: Israelis voted in record numbers on Tuesday, with turnout of about 77.7%, the highest in more than two decades, Rappler reports. France 24 says exit polls put the bloc led by opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot narrowly ahead of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's camp, 52 seats to 50, with neither side clearly able to form a government. Al Jazeera says Arab parties are projected to win a combined 18 [[knesset|Knesset]] seats, and President Isaac Herzog will choose the candidate he thinks best placed to try to form a government once results are in.
stories.background: This was Israel's first general election since the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October 2023 and the chain of conflicts that followed, and it was widely described as a referendum on Netanyahu's leadership.

stories.title: Lula wins a fourth term in Brazil; defeated rival Flávio Bolsonaro leaves for the US
stories.summary: Brazil's electoral court says Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Sunday's runoff with 51.78% of valid votes to 48.22% for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, MercoPress reports. Bolsonaro's party has accepted the result, but NPR says he has not conceded. Agência Brasil, citing Reuters, reports that he left for the United States after missing a deadline to hand over his passports in a money-laundering investigation, and that the Federal Police have revoked them. RTÉ says the US State Department will issue visas to him and his family. NPR adds that President Trump called the vote 'rigged' without offering evidence.
stories.background: Flávio Bolsonaro is the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. On Sunday night he said he would seek to annul the vote over the extension of voting hours, and the electoral court's president rejected that case on Monday, MercoPress reports.

stories.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 10,000 cases, with no approved vaccine for the virus behind it
stories.summary: DW reports that the Democratic Republic of Congo has recorded more than 10,000 Ebola cases and nearly 4,900 deaths, and that there is no approved vaccine or specific treatment for the [[ebola-bundibugyo|Bundibugyo]] virus causing it. NPR calls it a record-breaking outbreak that has spread with great speed. The BBC says Kenya has confirmed nine cases, and Euronews reports that the European disease control centre has sent experts to Nigeria, where a case has also been reported.
stories.background: NPR says the outbreak was first identified in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Health officials have been investigating how the first patients in Kenya and Nigeria may have been linked.

stories.title: Regional powers press Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz as another ship is struck
stories.summary: Qatar's foreign minister says it is now up to Tehran to show good faith, reopen the [[strait-of-hormuz|Strait of Hormuz]] and stop threatening its neighbours, while another ship was struck in the Strait, The Times of Israel reports. Euronews says Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey have also held talks in Tehran, and that Egypt's parliament approved military help for Saudi Arabia if it asks, as [[houthis|Houthi]] attacks threaten the kingdom. Al Jazeera says Iran's president, Masoud Pezeshkian, argued the Middle East can solve its own problems without the US.
stories.background: The US and Israel launched a war on Iran on 28 February 2026. Iran has blocked the Strait of Hormuz and targeted commercial ships, and the US has blockaded Iranian ports and oil shipments.

stories.title: A local ceasefire begins around besieged Oleshky while missiles hit Kyiv again
stories.summary: NPR reports that a local ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia took effect early Tuesday ahead of a humanitarian mission to Oleshky, a Russian-occupied town where residents have been eating weeds and pickles to survive, while missile attacks resumed on Kyiv. The BBC says the White House credited US first lady Melania Trump with securing the truce. The Kyiv Independent says a Russian ballistic missile hit Kyiv's Southern Bridge, leaving a large hole and closing it to road and rail traffic.
stories.background: Russia's full-scale invasion began in February 2022. The Kremlin has said three-way talks with the US and Ukraine could resume in mid-November, possibly in Abu Dhabi.

stories.title: Finland's and Norway's leaders phone Putin, splitting Nordic opinion
stories.summary: The leaders of Finland and Norway held a rare 90-minute call with Vladimir Putin, the BBC and Euronews report. Finland's president, Alexander Stubb, said ending the war in Ukraine 'will not be achieved through silence'. Euronews says the Danish and Swedish prime ministers publicly cast doubt on the move, and DW reports that Denmark's Mette Frederiksen criticised the two countries for not coordinating with allies, even though they had consulted Ukraine. The call came ahead of planned US-led peace talks.

stories.title: Serbia's student-led list wins a majority, ending Vučić's party's 14-year rule
stories.summary: Balkan Insight reports that the opposition Student List won an outright majority in Serbia's parliamentary elections, ending the 14 years in power of Aleksandar Vučić's Serbian Progressive Party. The BBC says Vučić said it was 'clear' his party had lost, and people celebrated in cities across the country. Scroll notes that the Student List has no single leader and fielded candidates without political experience from across Serbian society.
stories.background: The BBC says the student movement took just under two years to end the party's long political dominance. Balkan Insight reports that European leaders have welcomed the result and hope it will speed Serbia's progress towards EU membership.

stories.summary: A new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll shows Democrats with a slight edge with Election Day a week away, though NPR says lagging enthusiasm among key groups suggests gains may not come easily. The Times of Israel reports that the Iran war, now eight months old, has pushed up gas prices and left voters frustrated. At a rally in Texas, President Trump said he had been willing to go to war with Iran even if oil rose sharply, the Guardian reports. The BBC says Trump calls voter fraud 'rampant', while its fact-checkers say evidence suggests it is extremely rare.
stories.background: The midterms on 3 November will decide control of Congress for the last two years of Trump's term, according to The Times of Israel.

Colombia One reports that Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke about a US plan for Venezuela that includes changing its electoral infrastructure and calling elections.
stories.background: The BBC says Machado left Venezuela by speedboat a month before the US government seized President Nicolás Maduro.
